extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners filing or evaluating reexamination requests
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for deciding whether to grant or deny patent reexamination requests (ex parte and inter partes), including the standards for a "substantial new question of patentability" (SNQ) and a "reasonable likelihood that the requester will prevail" (RLP), and related procedural issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial new question of patentability (SNQ)
rubrics_metrics.description: The presence or absence of “a substantial new question of patentability” determines whether reexamination is ordered for reexaminations filed prior to September 16, 2011. A prior art patent or printed publication raises a substantial question of patentability where there is a substantial likelihood that a reasonable examiner would consider the prior art important in deciding whether the claim is patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For SNQ to be present: (A) the prior art patents/publications raise a substantial question regarding at least one claim (i.e., a reasonable examiner would consider them important), and (B) the same question of patentability has not already been decided by a final court holding, an earlier concluded Office examination or review, or raised in a pending reexamination or supplemental examination. A prima facie case of unpatentability is not required for an SNQ. If the same question has been previously decided or is pending, the SNQ is absent unless the prior art is presented in a materially different way (see "old art" guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable likelihood that requester will prevail (RLP)
rubrics_metrics.description: For reexaminations filed on or after September 16, 2011 and prior to September 16, 2012, the determination is whether the request and prior art establish a reasonable likelihood that the requester will prevail with respect to at least one challenged claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The RLP standard is an elevated threshold compared to the SNQ standard (House Report describes it as requiring information showing a reasonable likelihood of success). If a proceeding was terminated/vacated without resolving the RLP question, the issue can be re-presented in a new request. The Office must state in the granting decision that there is an RLP (for requests in this date range).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims considered in deciding request
rubrics_metrics.description: The claims of the patent in effect at the time of the determination (37 CFR 1.923) are the basis for deciding whether an SNQ or RLP is present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office's determination is generally limited to the claim(s) for which reexamination was requested. A requester must set forth the pertinency and manner of applying cited prior art to every claim for which reexamination is requested (35 U.S.C. 311(b)(2); 37 CFR 1.915(b)). Failure to apply the art to certain claims means the requester is not statutorily entitled to reexamination of those claims; failure to comply with 1.915(b) may result in no filing date being awarded. The examiner may nevertheless base an SNQ/RLP on claims other than those requested (e.g., claims in effect at determination time). The decision should discuss all requested claims, but the examiner should not reject claims in the order for reexamination (rejections belong in the first Office action).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to set forth pertinency and manner of applying cited prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: A requester must 'set forth the pertinency and manner of applying cited prior art to every claim for which reexamination is requested' (35 U.S.C. 311(b)(2); 37 CFR 1.915(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the requester fails to apply the art to certain claims, those claims generally will not be reexamined. A request failing to set forth the pertinency and manner of applying cited art may not be given a filing date. Thus each cited reference must be applied to each claimed element/claim that requester seeks to challenge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of previously cited/considered art ('old art') as basis for SNQ
rubrics_metrics.description: Reliance on previously cited/considered art ("old art") does not necessarily preclude an SNQ for reexaminations ordered on or after November 2, 2002. Determinations are fact-specific and may be based solely on old art if it is being presented/viewed in a new light or in a different way because of a material new argument or interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When old art is used as the sole basis for SNQ, include the form paragraph (¶ 22.01.01) in the order and explain how the old art is being applied in a new way. Examiner notes: insert the old art, explain how it applies (e.g., new interpretation), and use the form paragraph only the first time the already-cited art is applied. See Ex parte Chicago Rawhide Mfg. Co. as example.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior adverse decisions by the Office on same or substantially identical prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: A prior Office decision adverse to the patentability of a claim based upon prior art patents or printed publications would usually mean that a substantial new question of patentability is present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such adverse decisions could arise from a reissue application abandoned after rejection without disclaimer, or other Office proceedings. Examiner should consider prior Office adverse decisions when determining SNQ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior adverse reissue application final decision (grounds other than patents/printed publications)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any prior adverse final decision by the Director or the PTAB/board on an application seeking reissue of the same patent will be considered when determining whether an SNQ is present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, to the extent that such a prior adverse final decision was based upon grounds other than patents or printed publications, that prior adverse final decision will not be considered in determining whether an SNQ is present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior favorable or adverse decisions in other cases involving same art
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will consider decisions involving substantially identical patents or publications in determining whether an SNQ is raised; the weight accorded depends on the circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner discretion applies; look to the specifics of the other case(s) when deciding how much weight to give such decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of federal court decisions on SNQ/RLP determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal court decisions affect the SNQ/RLP inquiry differently depending on finality: (A) a final holding that a claim is not invalid does not necessarily preclude SNQ/RLP; (B) a non-final holding of invalidity/unenforceability is not controlling; (C) a final holding of invalidity/unenforceability after all appeals binds the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office makes an independent determination because courts and the Office may apply different standards of proof and claim construction. Where a claim was finally held invalid or unenforceable, the requester will not have SNQ/RLP as to those claims. Where court factual findings exist, the Office may accord deference to factual findings but is not bound except in the final-invalidity-after-appeals case. See Ethicon v. Quigg and In re Swanson for illustrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second or subsequent reexamination requests when reexamination is pending
rubrics_metrics.description: When a reexamination is pending and a second/subsequent request is filed, the presence of an SNQ depends on the art cited in the subsequent request. The subsequent request must independently provide a 'different' substantial new question of patentability with respect to the claims in effect at the time of determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the subsequent request includes the art that raised the SNQ in the earlier pending reexamination, reexamination should be ordered only if the new art raises a 'different' SNQ. If it raises the same SNQ, it is not new and should be denied. If different as to some claims but not others, grant in part. Once a different SNQ is provided for existing claims, the second request may also include info directed to proposed new/amended claims in the pending reexamination so the entire patent package can be examined without wasteful subsequent filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter partes subsequent-filing prohibition and extraordinary relief
rubrics_metrics.description: Once an order for inter partes reexamination has been issued, neither the third-party requester nor its privies may file a subsequent inter partes reexamination request of the same patent until an inter partes reexamination certificate has been issued, unless the Director expressly authorizes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prohibition (37 CFR 1.907(a); 35 U.S.C. 317(a)) tracks statute. Petitions for express authorization are requests for extraordinary relief and will not be granted if a more conventional avenue exists. Cantello v. Rasmussen illustrates the principle that extraordinary relief is disfavored if rules provide an avenue for relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of prior art considered in making the determination
rubrics_metrics.description: The determination of SNQ/RLP can be based upon any prior art patents or printed publications, 'with or without consideration of other patents or printed publications' (35 U.S.C. 312(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner is not limited to the prior art relied upon in the request; may consider other patents/printed publications of record or perform a limited search to supply deficiencies in the prior art cited in the request where there is a reasonable likelihood that prior art can be found to supply necessary deficiencies. Search should be targeted to areas most likely to contain the deficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content required in decision ordering reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: If a request for reexamination is granted, the examiner’s decision granting the request will state that an SNQ has been raised (for pre-9/16/2011 requests) or that there is an RLP (for requests between 9/16/2011 and 9/15/2012), and will include an order for inter partes reexamination where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision will (A) identify all claims and issues, (B) identify the patents/printed publications relied upon, and (C) provide a brief statement of the rationale supporting each SNQ/RLP. The order may be accompanied by the initial Office action on the merits, and if the order resulted from a petition, the subsequent inter partes reexam will ordinarily be conducted by a different examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination requests filed after reissue
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a request for reexamination is filed on a patent after a reissue patent for that patent has already issued, reexamination will be denied because the patent on which the request is based has been surrendered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reexamination of the reissued patent is desired, a new request based on the reissue patent's specification and claims must be filed. If the reissue issues after the filing of a request, see MPEP § 2686.03 for handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: SNQ is not equivalent to a prima facie case
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not necessary that a 'prima facie' case of unpatentability exist for an SNQ to be present; an SNQ could be present even if the examiner would not necessarily reject the claim as anticipated or obvious in view of the prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between the lower threshold SNQ (whether an examiner would consider the art important) and the higher standard of making a rejection; see In re Etter discussion. Examiners should not conflate the two standards when deciding to order reexamination.
